name: GA-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Austin Scott running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger raised only ~$19k with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~98%
model.rationale: Austin Scott is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by fifteen points, while Kelly Esti has raised almost nothing and has no outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican hold, so the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: Any late surge in challenger fundraising or unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the margin, though a real contest remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 8th District is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about fifteen points toward the GOP. Austin Scott, the incumbent, is running for reelection with more than $1.3 million on hand after raising over $1.1 million. His Democratic challenger, Kelly Esti, has raised under $20,000 and reports less than $2,000 in cash, with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Scott roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. With the incumbent advantage, the fundraising gap, and the district's lean all pointing the same direction, this is a safe Republican seat with little evidence of a competitive race developing.
